facts.statement: Mimodactylus lived in present-day Lebanon during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 95 million years ago.
facts.quote: Mimodactylus is a genus of istiodactyliform pterosaur that lived in what is now Lebanon during the Late Cretaceous, 95 million years ago.

facts.statement: The only known specimen of Mimodactylus was found in a limestone quarry near Hjoula in the Sannine Formation.
facts.quote: The only known specimen was discovered in a limestone quarry near the town of Hjoula, belonging to the Sannine Formation.

facts.statement: Mimodactylus libanensis was named by researchers in 2019.
facts.quote: In 2019, the researchers named the new genus and species Mimodactylus libanensis

facts.statement: The holotype specimen is the first complete pterosaur discovered from the Afro-Arabian continent.
facts.quote: The well-preserved holotype specimen is the first complete pterosaur from the Afro-Arabian continent

facts.statement: The holotype specimen had a wingspan of 1.32 meters.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen is comparatively small, with a wingspan of 1.32 m

facts.statement: Mimodactylus had a broad snout with cone-shaped teeth restricted to the front half of its jaws.
facts.quote: Its snout is broad and the cone-shaped teeth are confined to the front half of the jaws.

facts.statement: The teeth of Mimodactylus were sideways-compressed with a thickened base ridge but lacked sharp cutting edges.
facts.quote: The tooth crowns are compressed sideways and have a cingulum (a thickened ridge at the base), and lack sharp carinae (cutting edges).

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Mimodactylus may have foraged for decapod crustaceans on water surfaces, based on its unique teeth.
facts.quote: The teeth of Mimodactylus suggest its feeding habits differed from other pterosaurs. Possibly it foraged for decapod crustaceans from water surfaces.

facts.statement: Mimodactylus is classified in the clade Mimodactylidae, which includes Haopterus, and belongs to the larger group Istiodactyliformes.
facts.quote: The describers of Mimodactylus classified it in the new clade Mimodactylidae along with Haopterus, this group being part of Istiodactyliformes.

facts.statement: The specimen was collected from a private quarry near Hjoula, Lebanon, over fifteen years before it was scientifically described in 2019.
facts.quote: The only known specimen of this pterosaur was collected from a private limestone quarry near the town of Hjoula, Lebanon, more than fifteen years before its 2019 scientific description.

facts.statement: Kellner and colleagues formally named the species Mimodactylus libanensis in 2019.
facts.quote: In 2019, Kellner and colleagues named the new genus and species Mimodactylus libanensis

facts.statement: The genus name Mimodactylus honors the MIM Museum and combines it with the Greek word for 'digit'.
facts.quote: The generic name refers to the MIM Museum, in recognition of where the specimen is housed and according to the wishes of the philanthropist who acquired the specimen, combined with the Greek word daktylos (δάκτυλος) for "digit".

facts.statement: The holotype specimen is cataloged with the number MIM F1.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen is catalogued as MIM F1

facts.statement: The specimen was likely a juvenile when it died, as indicated by unfused bones.
facts.quote: It was probably a young individual when it died, based on some bones not being fused

facts.statement: Based on a 2015 system by Kellner, the specimen reached an ontogenetic growth stage between 2 and 3 out of 6.
facts.quote: This indicates the specimen had reached an ontogenetic (growth) stage between stages 2 and 3 out of 6, according to a system for determining the age of pterosaur fossils devised by Kellner in 2015

facts.statement: Mimodactylus was covered in hair-like pycnofibres and possessed extensive wing membranes supported by a long wing-finger.
facts.quote: As a pterosaur, Mimodactylus would have been covered in hair-like pycnofibres, and had extensive wing-membranes, which were distended by the long wing-finger.

facts.statement: Researchers described Mimodactylus as having a sparrow-sized body, a head longer than its body, and long, narrow wings, resembling 'wings with a mouth'.
facts.quote: In an interview, Caldwell described Mimodactylus as having long, narrow wings, but with a body the size of a sparrow, a head longer than its body, and being rather like "wings with a mouth".

facts.statement: The preserved skull of Mimodactylus measures 99 mm in length, while the preserved lower jaw measures 105 mm.
facts.quote: The preserved part of the skull of Mimodactylus is 99 mm long, and the preserved part of the lower jaw is 105 mm.

facts.statement: The first upper tooth of Mimodactylus was small with an almost circular cross-section, while the subsequent teeth were the largest in the upper jaw.
facts.quote: The first upper tooth of Mimodactylus is small, with an almost circular cross-section, and the following teeth are the largest of the upper jaw

facts.statement: The postpalatinal fenestra in Mimodactylus was elongated and egg-shaped, a feature also seen in Hongshanopterus.
facts.quote: The postpalatinal fenestra (opening behind the palate) is elongated and egg-shaped, as in Hongshanopterus.

facts.statement: Mimodactylus had a very short tail, evidenced by seven visible caudal vertebrae that quickly diminished in size towards the rear.
facts.quote: Seven caudal vertebrae of the tail are visible, which lack a duplex centrum, and quickly diminish in size towards the rear, indicating that the tail of this species was very short.

facts.statement: The scapula of Mimodactylus was 29 mm long, stout with a constricted shaft, and notably longer than the coracoid.
facts.quote: The scapula (shoulder blade) is 29 mm long. It is stout and has a constricted shaft, as in istiodactylids and anhanguerids, but differs in being somewhat longer than the coracoid (part of the shoulder girdle).

facts.statement: The humerus of Mimodactylus measured 52 mm in length.
facts.quote: The humerus (upper arm bone) of Mimodactylus is 52 mm long.

facts.statement: The deltopectoral crest of the humerus in Mimodactylus was distinctive for being rectangular with an unusual straight lower edge.
facts.quote: The deltopectoral crest of the humerus (ridge for attachment of the deltoid and pectoral muscles) is distinctive (an autapomorphy) in being rectangular, and has an unusual, straight, lower edge.

facts.statement: The ulna of Mimodactylus measured 84 mm in length.
facts.quote: The ulna (a lower arm bone) is 84 mm long.

facts.statement: The wing finger phalanges of Mimodactylus measured 128 mm, 119 mm, 105 mm, and 92 mm respectively.
facts.quote: The first wing phalanx is 128 mm long, the second 119 mm, the third 105 mm, and the fourth 92 mm.

facts.statement: The pteroid bone of Mimodactylus was large and measured 53 mm, making it longer than the humerus.
facts.quote: The pteroid bone (a hand-bone unique to pterosaurs which supported the front wing-membrane or propatagium) of Mimodactylus is rather large, and longer than the humerus at 53 mm.

facts.statement: The preserved femur of Mimodactylus was 36 mm long, significantly shorter than the humerus.
facts.quote: The humerus is much longer than the femur (thighbone), the preserved part of which is 36 mm long.

facts.statement: The tibiotarsus of Mimodactylus measured 60 mm in length.
facts.quote: The tibiotarsus (lower-leg bone) is 60 mm long.

facts.statement: Kellner and colleagues named the clade containing Mimodactylus and Haopterus Mimodactylidae within the group Lanceodontia.
facts.quote: The two genera formed a clade within the group Lanceodontia, for which they coined the name Mimodactylidae.

facts.statement: Mimodactylus was the first istiodactyliform discovered in Gondwana, whereas other members of the group were previously known only from Early Cretaceous sites in Europe and Asia.
facts.quote: They noted that Mimodactylus is the first istiodactyliform known from Gondwana (the southern supercontinent which included Africa and Arabia), members of the group previously being only known from Early Cretaceous sites in Europe and Asia.

facts.statement: A 2021 study by Jiang Shunxing and colleagues placed Mimodactylus in an unresolved polytomy with Haopterus, Yixianopterus, and Linlongopterus.
facts.quote: A 2021 study by the Chinese paleontologist Jiang Shunxing and colleagues found Mimodactylus in a polytomy (a group that is unresolved due to having more than two branches) with Haopterus, Yixianopterus, and Linlongopterus.

facts.statement: In 2022, Yizhi Xu and colleagues classified Mimodactylus as the sister taxon of Linlongopterus, with Haopterus at the base of their clade.
facts.quote: The Chinese paleontologist Yizhi Xu and colleagues found Mimodactylus to be the sister taxon of Linlongopterus in 2022, with Haopterus at the base of their clade.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul considered Yixianopterus to be part of Mimodactylidae in 2022.
facts.quote: The American palaeontologist Gregory S. Paul considered Yixianopterus part of Mimodactylidae in 2022.

facts.statement: Steven C. Sweetman noted in 2023 that Mimodactylus was the latest occurring member of Istiodactyliformes.
facts.quote: A 2023 article by the British paleontologist Steven C. Sweetman noted that Mimodactylus was the latest occurring member of Istiodactyliformes.

facts.statement: Researchers suggested in 2019 that Mimodactylus likely had unique feeding habits distinct from other pterosaurs.
facts.quote: Kellner and colleagues suggested in 2019 that it probably had different feeding habits.

facts.statement: Mimodactylus possessed a broad rostrum and widely spaced, robust, pointed teeth adapted for seizing shrimp in the water.
facts.quote: The broad rostrum and widely spaced, relatively robust, and pointed teeth of Mimodactylus would have been helpful for seizing shrimp in the water.

facts.statement: Researchers noted that while insectivory could not be ruled out, Mimodactylus's broad rostrum was consistent with a primarily crustacean diet, similar to extant ducks, boat-billed herons, and shoebills.
facts.quote: Kellner and colleagues noted that although insectivory could not be ruled out, the broad rostrum of Mimodactylus was consistent with a faunivorous diet, or primarily a diet of crustaceans, like in some extant ducks, boat-billed herons, and shoebills.

facts.statement: Mimodactylus lived about 95 million years ago during the late Cenomanian age of the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Mimodactylus is known from the Sannine Formation in Hjoula, Lebanon, which is dated to the late Cenomanian age of the Late Cretaceous, about 95 million years ago.

facts.statement: During the Late Cretaceous, Lebanon was mostly submerged on a shallow carbonate platform bordering the Afro-Arabian continent and the Neotethys ocean, though some small islands were exposed.
facts.quote: Lebanon was mostly submerged on a large, shallow carbonate platform during the middle Cenomanian, which bordered the northeastern part of the Afro-Arabian continent with the Neotethys ocean, but some small islands were exposed.

facts.statement: The Cenomanian climate in Lebanon was similar to the current Mediterranean region, supporting flora including pteridophytes, gymnosperms, and angiosperms.
facts.quote: The Cenomanian flora of Lebanon (which included pteridophytes, gymnosperms, and angiosperms) was similar to the contemporary fossil floras known from North America, Central Europe, and Crimea, and indicates a climate similar to that of the current day Mediterranean region.

facts.statement: Mimodactylus shared its habitat with another pterosaur, the azhdarchoid Microtuban, at the Hjoula locality.
facts.quote: Hjoula is known for its well-preserved fish fossils, but other organisms have been found there. One other pterosaur is known from the locality, the azhdarchoid Microtuban.

facts.statement: The species Mimodactylus libanensis was named and described in 2019 by Alexander Wilhelm Armin Kellner, Michael Wayne Caldwell, Borja Holgado, Fabio Marco Dalla Vecchia, Roy Nohra, Juliana Manso Sayão, and Philip John Currie.
facts.quote: En 2019, la especie tipo Mimodactylus libanensis fue nombrada y descrita por Alexander Wilhelm Armin Kellner, Michael Wayne Caldwell, Borja Holgado, Fabio Marco Dalla Vecchia, Roy Nohra, Juliana Manso Sayão y Philip John Currie.

facts.statement: The genus name Mimodactylus combines a reference to the MIM museum acronym with the Greek word daktylos, meaning "finger".
facts.quote: El nombre del género combina una referencia al MIM, el acrónimo habitual del museo, con un griego δάκτυλος, daktylos, "dedo".

facts.statement: The specific name libanensis refers to the animal's origin in Lebanon.
facts.quote: El nombre específico se refiere a la procedencia del Líbano.

facts.statement: The holotype, MIM F1, was excavated from a marine deposit of the Sannine Formation dating to the Cenomanian, about 95 million years ago.
facts.quote: El holotipo, MIM F1, fue excavado en un depósito marino de la Formación Sannine que data del Cenomaniense, de unos 95 millones de años.

facts.statement: The holotype consists of a relatively complete skeleton with skull and lower jaws, lacking some vertebrae and pelvic elements.
facts.quote: Consiste en un esqueleto relativamente completo con cráneo y mandíbulas inferiores. Carece de algunas vértebras y algunos elementos pélvicos.

facts.statement: The holotype represents a juvenile individual.
facts.quote: Es un individuo juvenil.

facts.statement: The holotype represents the most complete pterosaur skeleton ever found on the Afro-Arabian plate.
facts.quote: Representa el esqueleto de pterosaurio más completo jamás encontrado en la placa afroárabe.

facts.statement: The genus Mimodactylus was established by Kellner et al. in 2019.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Kellner et al., 2019

facts.quote: species: Mimodactylus libanensis

facts.quote: familia: Mimodactylidae

facts.statement: Mimodactylus is classified within the unranked family Istiodactyliformes.
facts.quote: unranked_familia: Istiodactyliformes

facts.statement: Mimodactylus is a pterodactyloid mimodactylid pterosaur that lived in the Late Cretaceous in what is now Lebanon.
facts.quote: Mimodactylus es un género de pterosaurio pterodactiloide mimodactílido que vivió en el Cretácico Tardío en lo que ahora es el Líbano.

facts.statement: Mimodactylus likely had limited maneuverability during flight but was highly stable, similar to albatrosses and other open-sea fliers.
facts.quote: The ability to manoeuvre during flight appears to have been limited in Mimodactylus as in open-sea fliers, and it was probably highly stable when flying, like albatrosses and some other birds.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that dynamic soaring, flying with little flapping, may have been the mode of flight for large pterosaurs including Mimodactylus.
facts.quote: Such dynamic soaring (flying with little flapping) may also have been the mode of flying of large pterosaurs such as anhanguerians, istiodactylids and pteranodontians.

facts.statement: Although the Hjoula deposits are marine, terrestrial fossils indicate the area was close to a paleoshore during the late Cenomanian.
facts.quote: Deposits of the Hjoula outcrops are marine, but terrestrial fossils indicate that it was close to a palaeoshore during the late Cenomanian.

facts.statement: The limestone of Hjoula is characterized as compact, soft, laminated rock that is light yellow or grey-yellow and lacks flint nodules.
facts.quote: The limestone of Hajoula is compact, soft, and laminated rock, which is characterised by being light yellow or grey-yellow, and in not having flint nodules.

facts.statement: Fish fossils found at Hjoula include the shark Cretalamna, the ray Libanopristis, the pachycormiform Eubiodectes, the polymixiiform Aipichthys, and the pycnodontid Nursallia.
facts.quote: Fish include the shark Cretalamna, the ray Libanopristis, the pachycormiform Eubiodectes, the polymixiiform Aipichthys, and the pycnodontid Nursallia.

facts.statement: Octopus fossils found at Hjoula include Keuppia and Styletoctopus.
facts.quote: Octopuses include Keuppia and Styletoctopus.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Mimodactylus was insectivorous, as insectivorous pterosaurs like anurognathids typically have slim, well-spaced, isodont teeth.
facts.quote: Insectivorous species often have slim teeth that can more easily break down arthropods, and among pterosaurs, anurognathids are thought to be adapted for this with their well-spaced, isodont (of equal length) teeth.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that despite having wider teeth, Mimodactylus may have been capable of breaking down arthropod exoskeletons.
facts.quote: Though Mimodactylus had wider teeth, they may otherwise have fitted this mode of feeding by being able to break down the exoskeletons of arthropods.

facts.statement: While insectivory cannot be ruled out, researchers note that Mimodactylus's broad rostrum is consistent with a primarily crustacean diet.
facts.quote: Kellner and colleagues noted that although insectivory could not be ruled out, the broad rostrum of Mimodactylus was consistent with a faunivorous diet, or primarily a diet of crustaceans, like in some extant ducks, boat-billed herons, and shoebills.

facts.statement: In 2019, Dany Azar and colleagues reported fossil dragonflies and a beetle from Hjoula, showing the site has potential for preserving insects.
facts.quote: The first two fossil dragonfly species from Lebanon (including Libanoliupanshania mimi, also named for the MIM Museum) and a beetle were reported by the Lebanese palaeontologist Dany Azar and colleagues in 2019, showing that Hjoula does have potential for preserving insects.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest there may be a taphonomic bias favoring the preservation of strong fliers at Hjoula.
facts.quote: There may also be taphonomic bias in favour of preserving strong fliers.

facts.statement: When Mimodactylus was described, insects had not been discovered at Hjoula and terrestrial plant fossils were very rare there.
facts.quote: Insects had not been discovered at Hjoula or the other Cretaceous Lagerstätten of Lebanon by the time Mimodactylus was described, and fossils of terrestrial plants are very rare at Hjoula.

facts.statement: An anonymous benefactor acquired a rare pterosaur skeleton and donated it to the Mineral Museum in Beirut, part of the Saint Joseph University of Beirut.
facts.quote: Un benefactor anónimo adquirió un esqueleto de pterosaurio raro y lo donó al Museo de Minerales en Beirut, parte de la Universidad de San José de Beirut.

facts.statement: The skeleton was prepared in Canada by Luke Allan Lindoe, a technician at the University of Alberta.

facts.statement: Since 2017, the museum has exhibited two life-sized models of the animal, one standing and one flying, along with a hologram.
facts.quote: Desde 2017, el museo exhibe dos modelos de tamaño natural del animal, uno de pie, el otro volando y un holograma.

facts.statement: The holotype of Mimodactylus had a wingspan of 132 centimeters, though the specimen was far from fully developed.
facts.quote: El holotipo de Mimodactylus tiene una envergadura de 132 centímetros, pero el ejemplar estaba lejos de estar completamente desarrollado.

facts.statement: The humerus of Mimodactylus features a rectangular deltopectoral crest.
facts.quote: El húmero tiene una cresta deltopectoral rectangular.

facts.statement: The palate possesses a distinct crest.
facts.quote: El paladar tiene una cresta distinta.

facts.statement: The upper jaws each have eleven teeth, while the lower jaws have ten.
facts.quote: Las mandíbulas superiores tienen cada una once dientes y las mandíbulas inferiores diez.

facts.statement: The scapula is slightly longer than the coracoid.
facts.quote: El omóplato es algo más largo que el coracoides.

facts.statement: The humerus is 30% longer than the femur.
facts.quote: El húmero es 30% más largo que el fémur.

facts.quote: La cresta deltopectoral cubre el 40% de la longitud del eje del húmero.

facts.statement: The snout of Mimodactylus is wide but not rounded at the front, ending in a sharp point.

facts.statement: The preserved length of the lower jaw is 105 millimeters.

facts.statement: It has ten teeth in the lower jaw, totaling forty-two teeth in the head as a whole.
